hsb_space.title: HSB Color Space
hsb_space.desc1: HSB expresses color using three axes: Hue (H), Saturation (S), and Brightness (B).
hsb_space.desc2: Hue is the angle on a color wheel (0–360°). Saturation is vividness and Brightness is lightness — each ranging from 0 to 1.

xyz_space.title: CIE XYZ Color Space
xyz_space.desc1: Designed from the response of three types of cone cells in the human eye. Only the Y axis represents luminance (brightness).
xyz_space.desc2: XYZ covers all colors visible to humans — wider than sRGB, including colors that cannot be reproduced on any display.

oklab_space.title: OkLab Color Space
oklab_space.desc1: OkLab is a perceptually uniform Lab-like space proposed by Björn Ottosson in 2020.
oklab_space.desc2: L is lightness (0–1), a is red-green axis, b is blue-yellow axis. Equal distances in OkLab correspond to equal perceived color differences.

oklch_lineage.title: Color Science Lineage
oklch_lineage.caption: Two branches from XYZ: CIE Lab and OkLab via cone responses.

oklch_vs_lch.title: LCH vs OkLCH Hue Rotation
oklch_vs_lch.caption: Equal hue steps in OkLCH appear more uniform in brightness.
